rationale: A durable correction rather than a new finding: the behaviour entry that describes ReadOnlySafe admission said each admitted request broadcasts a heartbeat, and the isolated-network receipt shows the cost is one heartbeat per peer, that is n-1 messages per request (64 for 32 requests in a three-voter cluster). Because that entry is used by the asserted read-index defect and by several interpretations that reasoned about retry cost, I am correcting its premise under the same id and naming the recorded uses that relied on the old reading, rather than adding a parallel entry.

knowledge.statement: ReadOnlySafe admission and growth, in this snapshot: every MsgReadIndex that reaches a leader is admitted individually. If the cluster is not a singleton and committedEntryInCurrentTerm holds, sendMsgReadIndexResponse adds one entry to readOnly.unconfirmedReads through readOnly.addRequest, which appends without any lookup of an existing request with the same context, and then calls bcastHeartbeat, which sends one heartbeat to every other tracked peer carrying r.readOnly.heartbeatCtx() - so one admitted request costs one heartbeat per peer, not a single message. If committedEntryInCurrentTerm does not hold, the raw message is appended to pendingReadIndexMessages and released only later, one response per queued message, each release again costing an admission plus a heartbeat per peer. Measured on a real three-node network with the leader isolated from both followers: 32 same-context requests produced unconfirmedReads length 32 with confirmedReads 0 and 64 heartbeat messages, one per peer per request.
knowledge.conditions: ReadOnlySafe, leader in StateLeader. Admission is per request and context-blind, so N retries with an identical context produce N entries; the outbound cost scales with N times the number of other tracked peers. Under a healthy quorum each retry is confirmed on the next heartbeat response, so the queue stays short. The node-level contract that makes retries the caller's duty is at node.go:218-224.
knowledge.changed_premise: The earlier revision said each admitted request broadcasts a heartbeat, which read as one message per request. Measurement and source show one heartbeat per other tracked peer per request, so the outbound amplification scales with the number of voters as well as with the retry count.
